title: Reading Test 7: Electric Buses and Urban Transport
passage: Electric buses are being introduced in many cities as transport authorities attempt to reduce emissions from public transport. Unlike diesel buses, electric buses produce no exhaust fumes while driving, which can improve air quality along busy routes.

The environmental benefit of electric buses depends partly on how electricity is produced. If the electricity comes mainly from coal, the total reduction in emissions may be smaller. If it comes from renewable sources such as wind or solar power, the overall impact can be much stronger.

Electric buses can also be quieter than diesel vehicles. This is useful in residential streets and near schools, where traffic noise can affect daily life. However, quiet vehicles may create new safety concerns for pedestrians who rely on sound when crossing roads.

Charging infrastructure is one of the main practical challenges. Bus operators need charging points at depots or along routes, and schedules must allow enough time for batteries to recharge. In cold weather or on hilly routes, batteries may lose energy more quickly.

Although electric buses can be expensive to purchase, their running costs may be lower because electricity and maintenance can cost less than diesel fuel and engine repairs. For many cities, the decision involves balancing high initial costs against long-term savings and environmental goals.

questionGroups.title: Questions 1-4
questionGroups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Choose TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

questions.question: Electric buses produce no exhaust fumes while driving.
Electric buses always have the same environmental impact regardless of electricity source.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 says the benefit depends partly on how electricity is produced.

questions.question: Quiet electric buses may create safety concerns for some pedestrians.
All electric buses can fully recharge in under five minutes.
questions.explanation: The passage discusses charging time but gives no specific five-minute claim.

questionGroups.title: Questions 5-7
questionGroups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C, or D.

questions.question: Which electricity source would strengthen the environmental benefit of electric buses?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 says renewable sources like wind or solar make the impact stronger.

questions.question: What is one main practical challenge for electric buses?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 identifies charging infrastructure as a main practical challenge.

questions.question: What does the final paragraph suggest cities must balance?

options.text: High initial costs, long-term savings, and environmental goals
School holidays and library opening hours

questions.explanation: The final paragraph states this directly.

questionGroups.title: Questions 8-10
questionGroups.instructions: Answer the questions below. Write no more than two words from the passage for each answer.

questions.question: What type of quality can electric buses improve along busy routes?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 says they can improve air quality.

questions.question: What kind of streets may benefit from quieter buses?
What kind of costs may be lower for electric buses?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5 says their running costs may be lower.
